With pytest, tests/test_convert.py can fail collection under lazy_loader>=0.4 ('No librosa.core attribute convert'); pre-import the submodule first: python -c 'import librosa.core.convert; import pytest; pytest.main([...])'.
issue_paraphrase: Passing a note name that carries a tuning deviation in cents (for example a note written with a -30 suffix) to the note-to-frequency conversion returns exactly the same frequency as the plain note name with no deviation, as if the cents suffix were ignored entirely. Anyone converting detuned or microtonal note spellings gets a silently wrong frequency back, with no error or warning, so the result only ever lands on the nearest equal-tempered semitone.
fix_summary: note_to_hz was forwarding **kwargs to note_to_midi, whose default round_midi=True quantized cents-bearing note names to the nearest MIDI pitch. The fix gives note_to_hz its own round_midi parameter defaulting to False and passes it through explicitly, preserving cent deviations by default.
notes: Deterministic, pure-Python, no network, no audio files; runs in well under a second. Verified env: numpy 2.5.3, scipy 1.18.1, numba 0.67.0, python 3.12.13. Note the note-parsing API is shared by several note-related functions; the fix only touches note_to_hz default behavior.

issue_paraphrase: Converting non-finite pitch values such as NaN or plus/minus infinity into note names crashes with an integer-conversion exception instead of returning a result, and converting an empty string the other way (back to a MIDI number) also raises an error. Vectorized pitch-processing pipelines that hit any missing, NaN or infinite value die mid-computation rather than getting a sensible empty result for the bad entries.
fix_summary: The note converters now handle degenerate inputs explicitly: midi_to_note (and the Indian-svara variants midi_to_svara_h / midi_to_svara_c) return the empty string for any non-finite midi value, and note_to_midi('') returns np.nan.

The fix commit also contains a large amount of annotation-only churn; the functional change is just the three guards.

python3 - <<'EOF'
import matplotlib; matplotlib.use('Agg')
import numpy as np, matplotlib.pyplot as plt
from matplotlib.colors import BoundaryNorm
import librosa.display
fig, ax = plt.subplots()
data = (np.random.default_rng(0).random((8, 8)) > 0.5)
img = librosa.display.specshow(data, ax=ax)
assert isinstance(img.norm, BoundaryNorm)
plt.close(fig)
EOF  # FAILS at parent (norm is a plain Normalize), PASSES at fix
observed_failure_at_parent: specshow on boolean data attaches a plain matplotlib Normalize(0,1) to the image, so a drawn colorbar spans the full continuous colormap (all intermediate colors) instead of only the two boolean levels; the plot is misleading. At the fix commit the image gets a BoundaryNorm(boundaries=[0, 0.5, 1]) and the colorbar shows just the two levels.
verified: Both directions observed with explicit resets and clean trees: at parent c7aa2ce8 the repro fails the isinstance assertion (norm type is Normalize); after `git reset --hard 6ee6e4fc && git clean -fd` the same repro exits 0 and type(img.norm).__name__ is BoundaryNorm. Fix present by inspection at the fix (is_boolean_cmap branch that setdefaults a BoundaryNorm) and absent at the parent (grep for is_boolean_cmap returns nothing). Caveat observed: the project's own pytest-mpl regression test (test_specshow_boolean_norm) PASSES at the parent commit too, because the pcolormesh pixels are identical; the discriminating oracle is the norm-type assertion above, not the image comparison.
install_recipe: git config --global --add safe.directory /work/librosa; git reset --hard <COMMIT> && git clean -fd; pip install -e '.[tests]'  (installs matplotlib >= 3.10.0 and pytest-mpl; no apt packages needed). Run the repro with the Agg backend; the pytest-mpl image comparisons additionally need a matplotlib version whose rendering matches the baseline PNGs (verified pass with matplotlib 3.11.1).
issue_paraphrase: When a 2D array of true/false values is plotted with the audio-visualization heatmap function, the colorbar that accompanies the image spans the whole continuous color ramp with many intermediate shades, even though the data are binary. The picture itself looks correct, but the scale makes binary data appear analog, which is misleading in figures and documentation.
fix_summary: specshow already chose a dedicated boolean colormap for boolean data; the fix detects when the inferred colormap is the boolean one (and the data dtype is really boolean) and injects a matplotlib BoundaryNorm with boundaries [0, 0.5, 1], quantizing colors to the two extremes of the colormap so the colorbar shows only the two boolean levels.
notes: No network and no audio files required; needs matplotlib (Agg is fine). Deterministic norm-type difference. Do NOT rely on the upstream mpl_image_compare test as the oracle (it passes at the parent too); assert isinstance(image.norm, matplotlib.colors.BoundaryNorm) instead. Verified with matplotlib 3.11.1, numpy 2.5.3. The fix hunk is ~14 lines in librosa/display.py.
